method: Untruncated2201..2800 source reading plus actual local clang preprocessor macro dump with XXH_IMPLEMENTATION and no optimization flag. Preprocessing full file is not credited as reading unread implementation.
findings: Actual default-selection code differs from broad memcpy-default documentation: GNU-compatible compilers generally select memory-access1 unless excluded older ARM condition. Method1 dereferences aligned1 typedef; method2 direct-casts; fallback memcpy. Configuration must be inspected before portability conclusions.

Local clang preprocessing confirms XXH_FORCE_MEMORY_ACCESS=1, XXH_FORCE_ALIGN_CHECK=0, XXH_SIZE_OPT=0, XXH_DEBUGLEVEL=0, XXH_NO_INLINE_HINTS=1 and XXH_VECTOR=XXH_NEON for this no-optimization translation unit. This is not a production-build configuration measurement.
XXH_NO_STDLIB makes allocation helper always returnNULL while free becomes no-op; it does not eliminate memcpy dependency. State allocation failure is expected under that mode.

Debuglevel0 maps assertions to assumptions/unreachable where supported; debuglevel>=1 uses assert which NDEBUG may disable. Invalid internal preconditions cannot be treated as cleanly returned errors just because assertion text exists.

Alignment checks default off on x86/aarch64 and size-optimized builds. Endian macro uses compiler target definitions or union-byte fallback; force overrides and cross-target behavior require separate tests.
Rotate fallback macros require nonzero count below word width and can evaluate arguments repeatedly. Compiler guards constrain optimization, not thread synchronization or runtime correctness.
